In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ag85B is an excellent candidate for inclusion in subunit vaccines, but it is not a good vaccine in itself.

Ag85B is a promising candidate vaccine antigen, and the identification of naturally derived T-cell peptide epitopes presented to Th1 CD4+ T cells by multiple HLA- DR molecules supports this conclusion.

the Ag85B protein is an immunogenic antigen, and the epitope repertoire presented to T cells from TB patients and BCG vaccinees is diverse, which is in accordance with the hypothesis that a subunit vaccine containing several epitopes from the Ag85B antigen would be more effective than a vaccine containing only one or a few epitopes.

we have identified naturally derived Th1-cell epitopes from Ag85B in the context of self HLA- DR molecules and have also demonstrated that these epitopes are promiscuously presented in association with multiple HLA- DR alleles.
